question: Should spawned-session chains receive a dedicated durable chain identifier and root key, or should the contract reuse or derive from an existing lineage concept?
rationale: Persisted session metadata and public projections are compatibility-sensitive, while current main already has distinct parent, session-rotation, and diagnostic lineage concepts whose intended ownership cannot be selected mechanically.

options.title: Dedicated spawn-chain identity
options.body: Add optional rootSessionKey and a purpose-specific immutable chain id derived when native or ACP spawn paths create a child.

options.title: Derive from parent links
options.body: Keep parentSessionKey and spawnDepth canonical, add traversal support, and avoid persisting a second chain identifier.

options.title: Reuse existing lineage identity
options.body: Bridge spawn ancestry to an existing trace or usage-family identifier after explicitly defining its lifecycle and cross-surface semantics.

recommendation.title: Dedicated spawn-chain identity
recommendation.body: Add optional rootSessionKey and a purpose-specific immutable chain id derived when native or ACP spawn paths create a child.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined signal from the issue review and recent ownership of the session/Gateway boundary.
